entry_conditions: Initial entry is the demonstrated open-finger rest state (qpos[7:9] about 0.040 m each). Supply the two causal 20 Hz raw observation frames; duplicate the first frame when no earlier observation exists rather than pass a fictitious zero pose. Mid-overlap entry is supported during handle pull, release, retreat, red approach, closure or initial lift. Reinitialize phase beliefs from qpos/qvel, TCP/red/blue world poses (metres, wxyz quaternions), drawer_position d in metres, drawer_velocity in m/s, and the one available pose change. For example at source 195, d is about 0.1863 m, drawer velocity about +0.107 m/s, fingers about 0.007 m each and TCP about [-0.3263,0,0.1279] m, consistent with an attached-handle pull. The actual network accepts neither prior commands nor a private predecessor latent. These observations are support cues, not hard acceptance thresholds or force/contact measurements.
exit_conditions: A supported late exit has d approximately 0.300 m, last demonstrated g=-1, qpos[7:9] approximately 0.0182 m each (total width about 0.03649 m), and red/TCP rising together near z=0.143 m. TCP remains about 0.009 m from red in x and approximately 0.001 m above its centre in the inspected lifts. This is initial red pickup, not completion of red evacuation. Earlier transfer can occur anywhere in the shared interval if the successor can finish that contact phase. Handle release at TCP z approximately 0.128 m with fingers opening toward 0.040 m each is intermediate, not a stop-all-motion exit. Drawer opening alone does not establish manipulation readiness. These guidance cues do not add conditions to the supplied drawer-open AND red-on-pad AND blue-inside task-success rule.
overlap_role: All assigned actions are learned, including the 279-281 shared actions starting at source index 195 and ending at the respective slice endpoints 474-476. The shared motion includes attached-handle pull to d approximately 0.300 m, release while TCP initially barely changes, open-finger upward retreat, free travel and orientation change toward red, downward red approach, closure while TCP again barely changes, and initial correlated red/TCP lift. Both adjacent policies are intended to learn this extended contact evolution; it is not collapsed to an instantaneous switch at d greater than 0.26 m. The diffusion action objective is applied throughout, without phase cropping or a scripted gripper transition.
successor_readiness: Pass the actual causal observation history in the same world frame and preserve the physical gripper state. Pass recent commands too if an external successor interface supports them, but no private phase posterior is required and this model cannot consume a command-history channel. The successor must infer whether to finish pulling, release and retreat, approach red, close, or continue initial lift. Do not reset g to open on switching. Closed fingers at roughly 0.007 m with drawer motion favor handle attachment; open fingers with retreating TCP favor free travel; fingers near 0.0182 m, TCP/red proximity and correlated upward motion favor red attachment. Attachment remains an inference. A useful late successor should continue red evacuation rather than repeat handle release or reopen fingers.
failure_signatures: Watch for inferred phase chatter, predictions consistent with free/open fingers while observed fingers remain near 0.007 m and the drawer is moving, a release before useful drawer opening, or inferred red attachment without correlated lift. Near-zero TCP velocity alone is ambiguous because the demonstrations pause both before closure and after contact. Gripper command and measured aperture differ during servo lag: demo1000 at 445 already commands closed with measured fingers still open. High posterior confidence is not calibrated on failures. These signatures are diagnostic guidance, not implemented hard safety checks or validated recovery logic.
continuation_guidance: Continue this policy while its observed phase is consistent with supported pulling, release, retreat, red approach or pickup and the successor is not yet selected. Replan with the fixed eight-action execution prefix; the policy does not choose its invocation duration or a preset skill schedule. At d greater than 0.26 m, still examine finger aperture and TCP/object motion: the policy has learned substantial remaining transition motion. When released, continue upward retreat and red approach rather than waiting at the handle pose. When near red, infer closure/lift from aperture plus TCP/red relation, not a global clock or low speed alone. Transfer by the demonstrated initial-lift endpoint, or earlier within overlap to a capable successor; continued large red transport beyond this slice is not trained here. Switching throughout the overlap is a proposed evaluation, not a performed test.
limitations: Observed evidence comes from successful training trajectories and measured expanded-slice boundaries, not trained-policy rollouts. The two-frame interface is shorter than the source heuristic's proposed 0.5-1 s command/observation memory. The learned GRU/filter is stateless across calls, initializes all phases as possible, and has uncalibrated censored age beliefs rather than measured event times. Duplicate frames are only an approximate history-mask signal. Ordered local phase transitions may inhibit retries; truncation augmentation is not proof of robust takeover. Geometry/future-co-motion labels are training proxies, future states never enter deployment forward, and no force measurement, IK, collision guarantee, invariance or missed-grasp recovery is implemented. Whole-task completion uses only the supplied completion contract and does not require extra release, speed, clearance or sustained-hold conditions.
